summary: Lumina Commerce: repeated failover oscillation causing streaming timeouts and customer-facing errors
description: Issue summary: Between 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC and 2026-03-10 05:40 UTC Lumina Commerce experienced repeated failover oscillations across their enterprise routes which caused streaming timeouts (client-observed stalled streams) and 5xx errors. Impact: multiple customer endpoints returned truncated streams or 504 timeouts, affecting live checkout conversational flows and resulting in a manual escalation to Redwood Support and SRE. Scope: ~1200 requests/min for Lumina's tenant during the window, with a tail of repeated retries that amplified autoscaler activity and route flapping. This ticket captures the incident timeline, investigation notes, immediate mitigations, and planned follow-ups for the customer and internal teams.
timeline: 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC: First error spike detected by customer alert (Lumina) showing elevated streaming stalls and client timeouts.
2026-03-10 03:16 UTC: Automated monitoring (Datadog) raised SLO error budget alert for Lumina enterprise route (errors > 5% for 5m).
2026-03-10 03:20 UTC: Support (Maya C.) acknowledged customer and opened incident channel (#inc-lumina) on Slack; Pager notified SRE on-call.
2026-03-10 03:30 UTC: SRE observed rapid autoscaler scale-out then immediate scale-in cycles for the dedicated GPU pool serving Lumina.
2026-03-10 03:45 UTC: Evidence of circuit-breaker tripping at the per-route proxy layer causing requests to reroute to fallback model variants.
2026-03-10 04:05 UTC: Short-lived canary that had been rolled out earlier that morning was rolled back (related PR #4432) after correlation with increased 5xx rates.
2026-03-10 04:20 UTC: Mitigation: temporarily disabled tenant-priority routing and increased circuit-breaker thresholds for Lumina route.
2026-03-10 04:50 UTC: Errors decreased to baseline and streaming success rate returned to expected levels for Lumina.
2026-03-10 05:40 UTC: Incident marked as contained; continued monitoring and follow-up actions scheduled.
2026-03-14: Post-incident review completed and remediation work items assigned.
investigation_notes: Metric snapshot: request rate ~1.2k RPS for tenant, median latency stable but p99 token latency spiked during scale transitions.

Autoscaler log snippets: saw repeated scale decisions within cooldown window; scale-in executed despite active inflight requests due to heuristic bug in cooldown computation (issue traced to autoscaler v2.1.0).

Circuit-breaker behavior: per-route proxy computed error rate using short window (10s) and triggered failover to cheaper model variant; combined with autoscaler oscillation this produced route flapping.
Control-plane signals: control-plane throttled some route updates during high churn, which delayed cleanup of ephemeral routing entries and extended failover time.

Canary correlation: deployment PR 4432 introduced a kernel selector tweak that altered latency distribution for short sequences; canary exposed a pathological interaction with our continuous-batching heuristic under Lumina's request shape.
KV-cache impact: no evidence of KV corruption; cache miss rate rose transiently during scale thrash, contributing slightly to token latency.
Supporting logs and dashboards: Grafana panels (dashboards/tenant-lumina) and Datadog traces (trace-id examples provided to customer) attached.
Hypothesis: combined effect of an aggressive scale-in heuristic, a short-window circuit-breaker, and the canary latency shift created a feedback loop amplified by client retries.
mitigations: Disabled tenant-priority routing for Lumina to remove preferential reroute pressure.
Raised circuit-breaker thresholds from 10s window to 60s window for enterprise tier as an immediate safety guard.
Applied a hotfix to autoscaler cooldown calculation to prevent scale-in within active-inflight requests (hotfix PR merged to autoscaler repo).
Rolled back the canary kernel selector change that correlated with latency shift (PR reverted).
Provisioned temporary additional reserved capacity in us-east dedicated pool for Lumina while long-term fixes are implemented.
resolution: Root cause: a feedback loop caused by (1) an overly aggressive autoscaler scale-in heuristic, (2) a short-window per-route circuit-breaker that triggered fallback to cheaper model variants, and (3) a canary kernel selector change that changed short-sequence latency. Immediate resolution involved disabling tenant-priority routing, increasing circuit-breaker windows, hotfixing the autoscaler cooldown logic, and reverting the canary. Customer-facing errors returned to normal and we provided Lumina with a detailed timeline and credit for impacted token usage.
follow_up_actions: Engineering: implement a scalable cooldown safeguard in autoscaler to consider inflight request counts (owner: infra/autoscaler, ETA: 2026-03-28).
Runtime: add a per-tenant circuit-breaker tuning profile for enterprise customers to avoid short-window thrash (owner: serving-runtime, ETA: 2026-04-04).
Product: update canary rollout checklist to include short-sequence latency regression checks for kernel selector changes (owner: product/console, ETA: 2026-03-21).
SRE/Support: create a runbook for tenant-priority routing toggles and add a fast path for emergency capacity reservations (owner: SRE, ETA: 2026-03-18).
Customer Success: schedule a technical review with Lumina to walk through findings and remediation; propose a 3-month monitoring plan and bill credit (owner: CS, ETA: 2026-03-17).
